clue.text: Surviving letter to the Corinthians that's unknown within New Testament

parts.note: a Greek letter, as the Corinthians would write
x is the algebraist's unknown
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A scholar notes which of Paul's letters to Corinth still survives in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at St Paul's epistles to Corinth; the 'letter' is a single character of the Greek alphabet the Corinthians wrote in.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant documents are those that have survived to the present.

clue.text: One of the horses departs after stock's reduced

parts.note: EQUIP (stock, as a verb: to supply) minus its last letter
d = departs, as on a timetable

explanation.surface: A stable runs low on feed and one of its horses is sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is a verb here: to stock a shop is to equip it.
explanation.definitionFit: An equid is any member of the horse family, so one of the horses.

clue.text: Seafarer with apostolic brief that may help him weather the storm

definitions.text: that may help him weather the storm

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: kept brief, the word about the apostle loses its last letter

parts.note: Pauline means of St Paul the Apostle

explanation.surface: A sailor carries a short letter from an apostle that might see him through a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apostolic brief' looks like a papal brief, but it is PAULINE (of St Paul) cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a waterproof canvas sheet used on ships to keep out rain and spray.

clue.text: Service vehicle pulled up on side of motorway

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the end side of motorway gives its last letter

parts.note: last letter of motorway

explanation.surface: A service vehicle has pulled over on the hard shoulder of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service vehicle' reads as one phrase; split it, and Service is the armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Senior Service is Britain's navy, one of the armed forces known collectively as the services.

clue.text: Cat chased by dogs, possibly very fast ones

indicators.note: what is chased has its pursuers behind it

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip
dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: A cat is chased by dogs, some of which are very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is the cat o' nine tails, a whip; nothing feline about it. Whippets are the racing dogs the surface half-promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippets are slim racing dogs bred for speed.

clue.text: Husband may put up with pony for a term (e.g. pony as horse)

indicators.note: with pairs the new piece with the swap that follows, bringing the pony into the word
one thing for another means a swap: the pony goes in where the A was
in a down clue, putting something up writes it from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A husband seems to tolerate a pony, followed by a bracketed grammar example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'put up' is a reversal in a down clue and 'with ... for a' swaps the pony in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyponym is a word for a narrower kind within a broader category, as pony is one kind of horse.

clue.text: Pants erupt with smell becoming foul

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the smell word is added after the rearranged letters
British slang pants means rubbish or poor, so the letters of erupt are in a bad state and rearranged

parts.note: a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Someone's trousers suddenly give off a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for underwear (pants are underpants in Britain) but is British slang for rubbish, telling you to rework the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrescent describes something in the process of rotting, so it is turning rotten and smelly.

clue.text: Inaccessible place for brooding heroine touring India

parts.note: Jane Eyre, Charlotte Brontë's heroine
India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A moody heroine travels round India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooding' seems to describe the heroine's mood; it belongs to the definition, where birds brood their eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a crag where the birds brood their young.

clue.text: Baseball infielder's two items of clothing

parts.note: first item: shorts
second item: a top

explanation.surface: A baseball player's kit is described in terms of what he wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The two garments simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop fields between second and third base, an infield position.

clue.text: Heartlessly knock down powerless friend — no longer buddy?

parts.note: FLOOR (knock down) without its central O
PAL without P (power)

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a weakened friend and is no longer his buddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddy' reads as mate, echoing 'friend'; here it means in bud, so something no longer in bud has come into flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant no longer in bud is in flower, and floral means of flowers.

clue.text: Take apart a French composer

parts.note: un is French for a
Maurice Ravel, French composer

explanation.surface: A critic dissects a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A French composer' reads as one phrase; the article is French too.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel something is to pull it apart thread by thread.

clue.text: Small marsupial droppings collecting round hill

indicators.note: the droppings word gathers the other pieces into itself

parts.note: poo is animal droppings
O is round in shape
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A little marsupial's dung piles up around a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small Australian rat-kangaroo, a hopping marsupial.

clue.text: Take in room in hospital round

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way

parts.note: a ward is a hospital room

explanation.surface: A patient is taken into a hospital room on the doctor's round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a ward round; it is only the instruction to turn WARD back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the breathing sense: you draw breath or take in air.

clue.text: Parisian is by mountains in Australia in colourful outer layer

indicators.note: by means next to, so the French word sits beside the mountain piece
the mountains word sits within the Australia word

parts.note: Oz is a colloquial name for Australia
a range is a chain of mountains
est is French for 'is', the word a Parisian would use

explanation.surface: A Frenchman stands by a mountain range in Australia, inside some brightly coloured rind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian is' asks for the French word for 'is', a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer coloured peel of citrus fruit, and on an orange it is bright orange.

clue.text: Person orchestrating hypnotism set to start with suspect

indicators.note: only the first letter of set is taken

parts.note: first letter of set

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is setting up a hypnotism session, starting with a suspect under interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set to start with suspect' reads as a plan to begin with a suspect; the phrase actually breaks after 'with', so 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a symphonist writes symphonies, scoring the parts for a full orchestra.

clue.text: Better half of pop song a hit in language of SW India

parts.note: pop is father; his better half is mother, MA
a lay is a song or ballad
as printed
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A pop song half of which became a hit in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half of pop song' reads as the stronger half of a record; 'pop' is dad, and his better half is MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam is the Dravidian language of Kerala, in south-west India.

clue.text: Scots are unaware of packages Southern Post Office delivered in error

indicators.note: to package is to wrap up, so the Scots word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: misken is a Scots verb meaning to be ignorant of or fail to recognise

explanation.surface: Scottish people are ignorant of parcels that a Post Office in the south sent to the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packages' reads as a noun for parcels but is the verb, the Scots word wrapping around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Words misspoken are uttered wrongly, so the speech was given mistakenly.

clue.text: French oil producer having Renault's front end checked by dipstick

parts.note: both are slang for a fool

indicators.note: the front end of Renault is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Renault

explanation.surface: A French car's oil is checked with a dipstick.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil, Renault and dipstick all say car maintenance; the 'oil producer' is a painter in oils, and dipstick is slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape painter who worked in oils.

clue.text: The knowhow to drive land yacht?

parts.note: a road is the land route, as opposed to sea
a yacht is an example of a craft; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what skill you would need to steer a yacht on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land yacht' is a real sand vehicle, which makes the phrase look whole; the question mark says yacht is only one example of a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadcraft is the skill and judgement of driving well on the road.

clue.text: First light turning ornamental cherry tree leaves red to begin with

indicators.note: leaves as a verb: the letter goes away from the reversed tree name
turning round makes the tree name read backwards

parts.note: Prunus is the genus of cherries, plums and their ornamental relatives

indicators.note: only the starting letter of 'red' is wanted

explanation.surface: At dawn a decorative cherry tree is changing colour, its foliage going red first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage in this autumnal picture, but it is a verb. PRUNUS reversed is SUNURP; R, the first letter of 'red', leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment of sunrise, when the day's first daylight appears.

clue.text: Retired fireman working with a special buzzer on the wall?

indicators.note: retiring means going back

parts.note: Fireman Sam, the children's TV character
on = working, as a machine
standard abbreviation
as printed
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A retired fireman takes a job fitting a special alarm buzzer to a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer on the wall' sounds like a doorbell or alarm; the buzzer is an insect, and the question mark flags the wordplay on its mud nest built on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Mason wasps build nests of mud, often on walls, and buzz.

clue.text: Monsieur visiting his dear one who perhaps arranged their meeting

parts.note: M. is the French abbreviation for monsieur
at = visiting, as in at the Smiths'
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A Frenchman visits his sweetheart, and someone wonders who introduced them.
explanation.walkthrough: The French theme runs through: M and CHER are both French, for the Frenchman and his darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A matcher pairs people up, as a matchmaker might have arranged their meeting.

clue.text: Pomeranian dog quaffing river spray

parts.note: the Pomeranian is a type of spitz
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A little Pomeranian laps at a river and sprays water about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pomeranian is one of the spitz family of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from German spritzen: a spritz is a quick squirt or spray, of perfume or water.

clue.text: Possibly flyer's getting new blue cape

parts.note: a flyer is one kind of promo, a promotional leaflet
standard abbreviation
blue is the colour of the Conservative (Tory) party in Britain

explanation.surface: An aviator is kitted out with a new blue cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests an airman and 'cape' a garment; the flyer is a leaflet, and the cape is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland jutting into the sea, as a cape does.

clue.text: Primate managed to intercede in self-inflicted blunder

parts.note: an own goal (OG) in football, a self-inflicted blunder
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A church leader steps in after someone's own blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' can mean an archbishop, which fits the interceding; here it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang, short for orangutan, is a great ape, a primate.

clue.text: Leave hastily from self-catering apartment on vacation

parts.note: S/C is the abbreviation in holiday listings

indicators.note: apartment is vacated, emptied of its middle

parts.note: first and last letters of apartment

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers flee a self-catering flat in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as on holiday, which the self-catering flat encourages; it means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is an order to go away quickly, so to leave hastily.

clue.text: One of several sharp nails left alongside fences

indicators.note: the phrase fences the answer in, enclosing it

parts.note: the letters run from the last of left into the start of alongside

explanation.surface: Some sharp nails are left lying beside a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fences' looks like the noun, somewhere to leave nails; it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is one of the sharp claws of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Deride junior ingesting double dose of ecstasy

indicators.note: taking in, so the junior abbreviation swallows the doubled letters
a double dose means two helpings, so the ecstasy letter is given twice

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a youngster who has swallowed two lots of a party drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or taunt someone with scornful shouts.

clue.text: Bats vanish after entrance of knight errant

indicators.note: the entrance of knight is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of knight

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: anagram of VANISH

explanation.surface: Bats disappear as a knight errant enters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight errant' is a set phrase, but 'errant' is the definition on its own. Bats is the crazy adjective, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant can mean straying from what is right, and knavish means dishonest.

clue.text: Elation about little piggy's growth?

indicators.note: the letters of elation are moved about

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Delight over a little pig putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The little piggy is a toe, from the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market' played on a child's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail grows on a toe, the little piggy of the rhyme.

clue.text: Worthless loco finally retired from sweet old railway

indicators.note: something retired from has withdrawn and is gone, so that letter leaves the sweet

parts.note: nougat is a chewy sweet

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of loco

explanation.surface: A locomotive has finally been withdrawn from a quaint old line, deemed of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet old railway' sounds like a pleasant heritage line, but 'sweet' is a confection, and 'old' and 'railway' are separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or importance, or futile.

clue.text: British School of Language in Rennes

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A British school teaches a language spoken in Rennes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rennes is the capital of Brittany, where Breton is spoken.
